qr-code-scanner.formula:
Decode = find 3 finder patterns -> determine grid version -> sample modules -> Reed-Solomon error correction -> extract bytes -> decode text.
This tool uses the browser's native BarcodeDetector API for the whole pipeline.
howTo: Upload a photo, screenshot, or image file containing a QR code.
Or tap Start camera, allow access, and tap Capture with the code in frame.
The decoded text appears in the result box.

keyFacts: A QR code stores text or a URL in a square grid of black and white modules.
Decoding finds the three square finder patterns, reads the grid, and corrects errors mathematically.
This tool decodes with the browser's built-in BarcodeDetector API. No library download, no server.
It reads QR codes from uploaded images and from your live camera.
Decoded text is shown only. The tool never opens links automatically.

mistakes: Trying it in Safari or Firefox — on-device decoding only works in Chrome and Edge. Other browsers simply can't decode yet.
Uploading a blurry or cropped photo — if the three finder squares aren't fully visible, there's nothing to decode. Use a sharp, complete image.
Opening the decoded link without checking it — QR codes can point anywhere. Read the URL before you tap through.
Expecting the camera to work over plain HTTP — browsers require HTTPS for camera access. Use the secure site address.
Cropping the code too tightly — cutting off the quiet zone around the code makes it undecodable. Keep white space around it.
